quality_summaries.rewritten_summary: Taiwan Insight (25 Feb 2026): Taiwan's 2008 Ministry order still requires sex-reassignment surgery to change one's registered gender, a requirement the article says blocks an estimated 90% of transgender people from obtaining national ID matching their gender identity, making every ID-dependent interaction - from clinic registration to airport security - a potential site of distress and discrimination. The Ministry of Health and Welfare has recognised gender self-determination as a human right since 2013, and Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 following Judicial Yuan Interpretation No. 748 (2017), but no substantive reform of the surgery requirement has followed; TAPCPR's strategic litigation continues to contest the surgery requirement in court.

Taiwan Insight (16 Jan 2026): during 2025 the Taiwanese government made no tangible policy change on abolishing the surgery requirement for legal gender change or on assisted reproduction, while pending changes to conscription criteria could actively harm transgender people. Anti-gender movement activity rose over the year: organisations echoed US anti-trans rhetoric, Taiwan's largest and most active anti-gender group (No Self ID Taiwan) published a translation of the US 'Keeping Men Out of Sports' executive order, and the Taiwan Solidarity Party pushed an official 'only two genders' position; TAPCPR and civil society groups continued to call for the abolition of compulsory surgery.

Taipei Times (19 Aug 2024): the Ministry of Environment will invest NT$280 million (about US$8.76 million) over four years to double the number of gender-neutral public bathrooms nationwide from 623 to 1,246 by 2029. Of transgender and gender-neutral respondents to the Gender Equality Committee's LGBT survey, 17% reported experiencing discrimination or fraught situations in public restrooms or changing rooms, and about 69% of all respondents said they have no problem with gender-neutral facilities.

Focus Taiwan (20 Nov 2025): an LGBTQ+ rights group reported that only 5 of the 149 government-listed all-gender restrooms recently inspected across Taiwan met the required standards, including clear signage indicating the facilities are open to all genders. The full CNA story is held in the CNA English news archive.

New Bloom (11 Nov 2024): strategic-litigation plaintiff Lisbeth Wu changed her legal gender on 8 October 2024 without submitting proof of sexual-organ-removal surgery, after the Taipei High Administrative Court ruled favourably on 26 August 2024; six rulings against compulsory surgery came from the Taipei and Kaohsiung High Administrative Courts in late May and mid-July 2024. Publicising Wu's change triggered a wave of anti-gender discourse on Taiwanese social media and more coordinated anti-gender movement mobilisation.

TaiwanPlus (15 Aug 2024): a Taipei court denied a transgender woman's request to change the gender marker on her government ID without requiring surgery or a psychological evaluation; the rights group supporting her case said it would likely appeal.

JURIST dispatch (4 Nov 2025): the 7th annual Taiwan Transgender March in Taipei on 24 October 2025 drew an estimated 3,000 people despite rain; participants called for an end to discrimination against transgender people and for abolition of the surgical requirement to change one's legal gender. The dispatch notes Taiwan's 2008 administrative ruling requires a diagnostic certificate signed by two psychiatrists plus proof of complete surgical removal for a gender-marker change, that no enacted legislation governs the process, and that Taiwan's courts have shown a generally positive attitude toward transgender rights.

Utopia Asia's Taiwan travel and resources page calls Taiwan 'one of Asia's most progressive countries for LGBT rights, and certainly the most liberal of the Chinese diaspora'; it records that Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage on 17 May 2019 following the Constitutional Court's 24 May 2017 ruling and regularised adoption for same-sex parents on 16 May 2023, and it lists LGBT organisations and venues across 12 cities. The page holds traveller-oriented practical listings rather than legal-risk analysis.

adds.title: Trans Teen Cannot Change Name, Mississippi Supreme Court Rules - Mississippi Free Press
adds.summary: Mississippi Free Press/AP (23 Apr 2025): on 17 April 2025 the Mississippi Supreme Court ruled 8-1 that a transgender teen undergoing gender transition cannot change his name, denying a petition filed nearly two years earlier by a then-16-year-old whose parents both consented. The majority opinion, written by Justice James D. Maxwell II, referred to the trans boy as a 'minor female' and cited the 2023 REAP Act - which bans both surgical and non-surgical treatments for transgender minors - as Mississippi's express public policy against children receiving life-altering gender-transition assistance; a chancellor may grant a minor's name change only where clearly in the child's best interest. Dated state-court confirmation of Mississippi's judicial posture on gender-transition recognition.

adds.title: Anti-Trans Bathroom, Sex Bills Die in Mississippi Legislature - Mississippi Free Press
adds.summary: Mississippi Free Press (1 May 2024): two anti-trans bills died in the Mississippi legislature after House and Senate lawmakers failed to reach agreement on compromise versions by the 29 April 2024 deadline - the 'SAFER Act,' which would have restricted transgender people's use of public bathrooms, locker rooms and public university dormitories (and which a House majority had previously supported), and the 'Women's Bill of Rights,' which would have codified a binary definition of sex as determined at birth into state law and curtailed legal recognition of transgender people's gender identities. Dated evidence of the 2024 legislative attempt at adult facility and sex-definition restrictions in Mississippi, which did not pass that session.

adds.title: Safe States Don't Make People Safer - The Needle
adds.summary: The Needle (16 Jul 2026), a state-by-state analysis of killings of trans women (per 100,000 trans women per year, 2008-2025, adjusted for undercounting): for Mississippi it records 6.6 such killings per 100,000 annually, above the US general-population homicide rate of 6.0 per 100,000 which the article prints as a comparison line; the piece's headline finding is that law tiers do not sort violence - both worst-law and safest-law states carry high rates. Gives the record a dated violence-rate datapoint for Mississippi, distinct from the state's legal-risk tier.

adds.title: Birth certificate bill restricting transgender Oklahomans heads to the governor - KJRH 2 News Oklahoma
adds.summary: KJRH 2 News Oklahoma (6 May 2026): House Bill 1225, which would require a male or female designation on Oklahoma birth certificates and prohibit any changes with very little exception, headed to Governor Kevin Stitt's desk after passing its most recent vote 70-17. Authors said it is designed to strengthen the existing law being challenged in federal court by transgender plaintiffs including Tulsa resident Rowan Fowler, and the state Attorney General's office confirmed the bill clarifies that Oklahoma never permitted gender birth-certificate changes; critics called it further discrimination. Dated local coverage of Oklahoma's sex-at-birth document law while still pending the governor's signature.

adds.title: Bans on Transgender People Using Public Bathrooms and Facilities According to Their Gender Identity - Movement Advancement Project
adds.summary: MAP (25 Mar 2026), the Movement Advancement Project's national per-state tracker: Oklahoma is listed under K-12 school-facility bans, with enactments in 2022 and again in 2025, grouping it with the states that restrict transgender people's access to bathrooms and facilities matching their gender identity. For this record it confirms the two enactment years (2022 and 2025) behind Oklahoma's facility-use restriction.
